question: How can you resize a window using its corners or borders in Windows?

options.text: Click the middle of the window and press Ctrl.
Press Alt + Enter to auto-resize the window.
Drag the title bar to change the size.
Place the mouse pointer over a border or corner until it turns into a double-headed arrow, then drag.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Place the mouse pointer over a border or corner until it turns into a double-headed arrow, then drag**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Resizing a Window in Windows OS:** To resize a window in the **Windows Operating System**, the most common and effective method is using the borders or corners. When you position the mouse pointer over a window’s **border or corner**, it will change to a **double-headed arrow**. You can then **drag** the arrow to resize the window to your preferred size.
 
• This feature allows users to customize the window size for better multitasking and screen management.
 
• The **double-headed arrow** indicates that resizing is enabled, and it supports both vertical and horizontal adjustments depending on the border or corner.
 
• The method provides flexibility in resizing and works with almost all applications in the Windows environment that support resizable windows.
 
• This feature is supported in most versions of **Microsoft Windows**, including **Windows 10** and **Windows 11**.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is to place the mouse pointer over a border or corner until it turns into a double-headed arrow, then drag.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Other Methods to Resize a Window:**

 
 
• Some applications allow resizing by dragging the **title bar**, but this only moves the window and does not resize it. *This statement is incorrect.*
 
• Using **keyboard shortcuts** like **Alt + Enter** may maximize or minimize the window but does not resize it. *This statement is incorrect.*
 
• Clicking the middle of the window or pressing **Ctrl** does not affect window resizing. *This statement is incorrect.*
 
 
 
• **Applications of Window Resizing:**
 
 
• Resizing windows is particularly useful for multitasking, as it allows users to adjust applications to fit their screen and work more efficiently.
 
• For example, resizing a browser window alongside a word processor makes it easier to reference information while working on a document.
 
• It is also helpful for **software developers** or designers who need to test applications or websites on different screen sizes.
 
 
 
• **Common Issues:**
 
 
• Some applications, like certain games or utilities, may have fixed sizes and do not support resizing via borders or corners.
 
• In cases where resizing does not work, users should check the application’s **settings** or ensure that the window is not maximized.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Features of Resizing:**

 
 
• Resizing is supported in most user interfaces that allow for dynamic window adjustments. This includes software like **Microsoft Office**, **web browsers**, and **file explorers**.
 
• The feature is critical for **accessibility**, allowing users to customize window sizes for better visibility and usability.
 
• Resizing is also essential when working on devices with smaller screens, such as **laptops** or **tablets**, where screen space is limited.
